title: Binary Authorization: only running an image that was signed

videos.script: Scanning writes a report. Nothing reads it when the image is deployed. {{report}} Binary Authorization is the part that reads. A policy names the signatures an image must carry. Without them, Cloud Run or GKE refuses to run it. {{policy}} It does not inspect the image. It checks signatures, over one exact digest. {{digest}} You will sign the shop's image on your own computer, with an open-source tool called cosign. Then you will push over the tag, and watch the check find no signature at all. {{cosign}} Last, who signs and when. Each signature stands for one decision. And whoever holds the key can admit anything. {{key}}
